programmes.name: Arabic

courses.title: Grammar I
skills_learned: explain types of Arabic sentences and word order therein
distinguish various types of Arabic tenses
analyse types of Mansbt and Marfct; and
to discover aspects of word case ending in Arabic sentences
courses.content_summary: Types of sentence in Arabic. Elements and factors in Arabic that affect the word order. Subjunctive word in Arabic (al-Mansbt and Appositives i.e. the Subject, Object of a sentence, `Ismu Inna and Khabaru Kna (at-Tawbc) for example: adjectives, affirmation, substitution and conjunction. Intensive study of the three Arabic tenses e.g. (Mdi Mudrc and `Amr)

courses.title: Language Drills I
skills_learned: read and comprehend Arabic texts
write short paragraphs
communicate and express himself in Arabic; and 4. demonstrate knowledge of Basic Arabic Grammar.
courses.content_summary: The course consolidates various aspects dealt with in ARA 101. It also entails extensive reading as well as comprehension exercises. Reading selected texts from poetry and prose. Answer questions about selected texts. Extensive exercises on writing short composition and summarizing texts.

courses.title: Study Skills
skills_learned: analyse Arabic texts
read and summaries Arabic texts
demonstrate knowledge of note-taking ,
making notes from resources and use the library; 5. use Arabic dictionaries and correct his notes; and
writing word without spelling mistakes
courses.content_summary: Areas of reading, note-taking, note-making, Summarizing, using the library, the dictionary. Intensive exercise will be given for illustration and testing the level of comprehension. Intensive exercise on writing difficult Arabic words specially writing: (Hamzat alwasl, Hamzat alqatc, Hamzah in the middle and at the end of word) other areas to be studied are: ( Att' almarbutah and att' almafthah, A

skills_learned: analyse meanings, types and characteristics of literature
appreciate relevant Arabic literary works
identify types of Arabic literature
differentiate characteristics of Arabic literature in various eras; and
identify the various schools of thought in Arabic Literature

courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
skills_learned: explain the concepts and theories of entrepreneurship, intrapreneurship, opportunity seeking, new value creation, and risk taking;
state the characteristics of an entrepreneur
analyze the importance of micro and small businesses in wealth creation, employment, and financial independence;
engage in entrepreneurial thinking
identify key elements in innovation
stages in enterprise formation, partnership and networking including business planning, and
describe contemporary entrepreneurial issues in Nigeria, Africa and the rest of the world
state the basic principles of e-commerce
courses.content_summary: Concept of Entrepreneurship (Entrepreneurship, Intrapreneurship/Corporate Entrepreneurship,). Theories, Rationale and Relevance of Entrepreneurship (Schumpeterian and other perspectives, Risk-Taking, Necessity and opportunity-based entrepreneurship and Creative destruction). Characteristics of Entrepreneurs (Opportunity seeker, Risk taker, Natural and Nurtured, Problem solver and change agent, Inn

courses.title: Digital Humanities: Application of Computer to the Arts
skills_learned: explain what Digital Humanities entails
appraise the DH techniques tools for data analysis
appreciate the importance of computers in the Humanities
apply DH to interdisciplinary research
appreciate the adoption of DH tools for entrepreneurship, and
apply DH to new research, publishing, media, networking
courses.content_summary: Meaning of digital humanities. Interface between computing and the disciplines in the Arts. Methodological and interdisciplinary scope of digital humanities. Techniques of data analysis; application of Computer in the Arts disciplines; entrepreneurial, research, publishing, networking and application of various digital tools; and the new media.

courses.title: The Arts and Other Disciplines
skills_learned: appreciate the relationship between the Arts and other disciplines
distinguish between interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary and trans-disciplinary research
assess the interconnectivity between disciplines, and
engage in interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary and trans-disciplinary research
courses.content_summary: Relationship between the Arts and other disciplines, e.g, Social Sciences, Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Medicine, etc. An investigation of the connection between the disciplines and the general intellectual terrain. Multidisciplinary, interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary interface of the Arts with other disciplines. Making connections across disciplines and perspectives.

courses.title: Grammar II
skills_learned: acquire knowledge of the evolution of Arabic grammar
identify some grammatical features related to nouns and verbs
analyse the Agent, the Vocative, Specification and Adverbs; 4. identify subject and predicate in Arabic sentences; and
formulate dual and plural nouns from singular
courses.content_summary: New Arts                                     36 Historical background of Arabic Grammar, grammatical features related to nouns and verbs, such as the primary and secondary signs of declension (calmt al-`Icrb) the Dual and its concomitants; the study of nominative and accusative nouns, such as subject and predicate, the Agent, the Vocative, Specification and Adverbs.

courses.title: Language Drills II
skills_learned: consolidate his ability to read and comprehend Arabic texts
acquire more knowledge of writing skills
improve his skills of note-taking; and
advance his ability to undertake independent search for knowledge in libraries and the internet.
courses.content_summary: This course is designed to consolidate aspects dealt with in ARA 201. It is also designed for the acquisition of advanced reading and writing skills. Selected texts of poetry and prose are to be studied for comprehension and dictations. Using of physical and virtual libraries should be advanced in this course.

courses.title: Texts from Pre-Islamic and Early Islamic Literature
skills_learned: study selected texts from pre and early Islamic literature
demonstrate knowledge of different types of literature in the period
identify distinctive contribution of Qur'n to development of Arabic Language; 4. identify contribution of adth to development of Arabic Language; and
analyze texts from pre and early Islamic eras
courses.content_summary: A textual study of selections from such literary genres as poetry, proverbs, wise saying, folktales, soothsayers rhymed prose and sermons/ addresses. One of the ten famous preIslamic poems and another from the Islamic era should be studied, also one sermon from each of the two periods. Influence of Qur'n and adth on the development of Arabic Language should be emphasized.

courses.title: Introduction to General Linguistics:
skills_learned: acquire the basics of General Linguistics and its branches
identify components of General Linguistics
recognize the relationship between Linguistics and other fields of study; and New Arts                         37
explore the efforts of the prominent scholars of this science in the Western world, and the contributions of traditional Arab linguists and their modern counterparts.
courses.content_summary: An introduction to the study of General Linguistics; definitions and its branches; the emergence and development of linguistics since the nineteenth century; efforts of its prominent scholars in the Western world; the contributions of traditional Arab linguists and the modern ones.

courses.title: Morphology of Verbs
skills_learned: explain detailed Arabic verbal morphological analysis
identify the rules of morphological analysis
analyze derivation and formation of word in Arabic Language; and
analyze naked and compound forms of words as well as the particles of augmentation in a detailed manner.
courses.content_summary: Definition and meaning of morphology. The morphological scale in Arabic language. And detailed analysis of Arabic verbal morphology; aspects of naked and compound forms of verbs as well as the particles of augmentation.

courses.title: Arabic Literature in the Pre-Islamic & Early Islamic Periods
skills_learned: acquire general overview of the literature in pre and early Islamic Periods;
study and analyse some short poems from the two periods; , and 3 to acquint himself/herself with notable literary figures from this period.
courses.content_summary: General overview of the literature in the two periods, with some emphasis on the literary genres and figures; a detailed study of one of the seven odes; some short poems from such collections as Mufaddaliyyat, Hamsah and Jamharah.

courses.title: Contemporary Arabic Prose
skills_learned: comprehend the meaning of modern terminologies and expressions as may be cited in selections from modern literary journals and daily press; 2. appreciate relevant Arabic literary works; and
identify types of modern Arabic prose
analyse the concepts of peace, conflict and security
list major forms, types and root causes of conflict and violence
differentiate between conflict and terrorism
enumerate security and peace building strategies
describe roles of international organisations, media and traditional institutions in peace building; and
differentiate the role of languages in peace and conflict resolution
courses.content_summary: Textual study of terminologies and expressions from modern Arabic literary works, journals and daily press; Arabic TV channels for modern Arabic expressions. To study distinctive modern Arabic prose and the influence of present Arabic dialects on modern Arabic prose. Contribution of the social media and technology in general in advancing Arabic language. 300 Level GST 312- Peace and Conflict Resol

courses.title: Research Methods in the Arts
skills_learned: explain the meaning, usefulness and characteristics of research methods
enumerate the types and approaches to research in the Arts
identify the essential variables in research methods, such as research problem, formulation of objectives, sampling techniques, among other;
engage in field works to collect data
formulate good research proposal
conduct original research / Long essay at the final year; and
write a report of the Long essay/research project, devoid of plagiarism and other ethical issues. New Arts                                   40
courses.content_summary: Meaning and characteristics of research; research methods; types of research in the Arts disciplines. Approaches to research, problems, proposals, techniques of data collection. Analysis and interpretation. Criteria for determining good data and the use of library resources; archives, internet, audio visual aids, field work, interviews, questionnaires, observations and focused-group techniques. Re

courses.title: Grammar IV
skills_learned: attain understanding of certain grammatical features such as Numbers
differentiate types of Arabic pronouns, types of declension; and
develop the ability to analyse Intensification of Imperfect and Inflection of Defective Verbs
courses.content_summary: The study of certain grammatical features such Numbers, Pronouns, types of declension, the Jussive Mood, Verbs of Approximation, Intensification of Imperfect and Inflection of Defective Verbs.

courses.title: Semantics:
skills_learned: explain the meaning of semantics, its concept and development
identify the efforts of Arabic linguists in ancient and modern times in area of semantics studies;
develop the ability to analyse and discover some types of semantics in Arabic language
explain the relationship between signifier signified
appreciate aspects of multiplicity of meanings, such as synonymy, antonym; 6. identify elements of semantic fields; and
state the characteristics of taboo
courses.content_summary: Introduce the concept of semantics and its development over time; the efforts of Arabic linguists in ancient and modern; the relationship between signifier and signified; the differences between language and speech; the types of semantics development, its factors and features; aspects of multiplicity of meanings, such as synonymy, antonym and linguistic taboo.

courses.title: Introduction to Classical Arabic Criticism
skills_learned: identify the historical evolution and development of Arabic classical criticism
identify early efforts of scholars on Arabic criticism
recognize methods of early critics; and
criticize texts according to rules of Arabic Classical Criticism
courses.content_summary: Basic approach to Classical Arabic literary criticism and a survey of the development of Classical Arabic Criticism, laying special emphasis on AL-`midi's Muwzanah.

courses.title: The Novel I
skills_learned: explain the definition and History of the novel in Arabic
discover components of the novel, and
attain ability to study and analyse the Arabic novel
courses.content_summary: The definitions of the novel, History of the novel in Arabic; the study and analysis of a specific novel. To study in general the main elements of novel i.e. narration, plot, theme, setting and character and to apply them on the selected novel of the study.

courses.title: A Play I
skills_learned: identify the definition and History of a play in Arabic Literature
discover characteristics of a play
attain ability to study and analyse an Arabic play; and
discover components of play
courses.content_summary: The course entails definition of and History of play and the Arabic art performance in Arabic; characteristics and components of a play; the analysis a play in Arabic literature. The course includes the study of types of play and elements of play: Role and character, relationships, situation, voice, movement, focus, tension, space, time, language, symbol, audience, mood and atmosphere. And to appl

courses.title: Rhetoric I
skills_learned: explain a short historical survey of Arabic Rhetoric New Arts                  42

appreciate elements of Aeabic Rhetoric such as Similes, Metaphors of Arabic; 3 identify the three components of Arabic rhetoric i.e. (Albayn Badc and Almacn); and 4. analyse components of Arabic rhetoric in a selected text.
courses.content_summary: A short historical survey of Arabic Rhetoric, the "Bayn" and "Macn" Similes, Metaphors, `Ijz, Itnb, Isnd and Wal. The course includes the study of some founders of Arabic Rhetoric i.e. al-Jiz in his book albayn wa at-tabyin, Arrummni in his book Annawdir, Albqiln, Aljurjn, as-Sakkki and alqazwin.

courses.title: Prosody 1
skills_learned: expain the historical background to Arabic Prosody
identify the metres of prosody and their features in Arabic
identify efforts of Khall bin Ahmad on Arabic prosody, and
analyse Arabic poetry
courses.content_summary: Historical background of Arabic Prosody, "Zift" and "cIll" i.e. deviations and irregularities in Arabic metres of poetry. The Study and Analysis of the fourteen metres. Detailed study of the founding father of Arabic prosody: Alkhall bin Ahmad. Applied study of the metres of poetry on selected poems, the selection should include poetry of some Nigerian poets.

courses.title: Phonetics and Phonology
skills_learned: analyse the branches of phonetics and phonology of the Arabic Language
pronounce Arabic sounds correctly
identify aspects as morphemes, allomorphs, phonemes, as well as the sound system of Arabic Language; and
demonstrate knowledge of the language lab and its benefits in the study of sounds
courses.content_summary: Introduce the study of branches of phonetics i.e. Articulatory, Acoustic and Auditory phonetics and the study of phonology of the Arabic Language; consonant and vowels, morphemes, allomorphs, phonemes, as well as the sound system of Arabic. The Arabic Language Lab should be used to demonstrate Arabic sounds and pronunciation.

courses.title: Translation I
skills_learned: identify history and basic principles of translation
analyse qualifications of a translator
explain the steps of translation
types of translation; and
translate simple texts from and into Arabic
courses.content_summary: Introduce the students to the history and basic principles of translation. qualifications of a translator. Steps of translation. types of translation, and technicalities of translation in relation to Arabic and English languages. The importance of dictionaries in translation. Conduct intensive exercises in literary translation from and to Arabic.

courses.title: Methods of Research
skills_learned: identify the rules of academic research in Arabic studies,
acquire ability to design and carry out research and present an original piece of writing in the discipline;
undertake independent research work without supervision; and
identify the scientific methods of editing Arabic manuscripts
courses.content_summary: Expose special Honours students the modern methods of research in Arabic Studies, relationship between the student and his supervisor, the role of each one of them, how to write a research proposal, authentication of research resources and exposing them to publishing a research. To draw the attention of students to the danger of plagiarism and the scientific methods of editing Arabic manuscripts.

courses.title: Comparative Arabic Literature
skills_learned: define comparative literature, its development and establishment in Arabic studies
compare Arabic literature with others
study and analyse the influence of Arabic on other literary traditions
influence of other literary traditions on Arabic; and
identify influence of Arabic literature on Nigerian literary traditions in local languages
courses.content_summary: Development of comparative literature and its establishment in Arabic studies; basic ideas in comparative literature such as Arabic-Western Literary elations, the influence of Arabic on other literary traditions, translation theory, thematology, Literature and Religion, Literature and the other Arts. New Arts                                    44

courses.title: Information and Communication Technology for Arabic  (2
skills_learned: operate Arabic oriented computer hardware and software
use World Wide Web resources on Arabic language and literature and other Library potentials of the internet for Arabic studies as well as other ICT resources helpful in Arabic studies research; and
operate computer for his personal benefit
courses.content_summary: This course is to introduce student to components of computer, office productivity software, understanding spreadsheets, word processing, presentations and understanding databases. Arabic oriented computer hardware and software feature; survey of World Wide Web resources on Arabic language and literature; Library potential of the internet for Arabic studies as well as other ICT resources helpful i

courses.title: Grammar V
skills_learned: develop critical approaches to traditional Arabic Grammar
analyze the debate between the call for easing Arabic grammar and those who oppose this motion;
explain the evolution of Grammar Schools in Arabic; and
be exposed to some selected topics of Arabic Grammar, such as the Construct, the Appositives, exception.
courses.content_summary: The study of Schools of Arabic Grammar and their evolution in Kufa, Basra, Bagdad, Eygpt and Andalus. Modern critical approaches to traditional Arabic Grammar as contained in such works as Ibrahim Mustafa's `Iy' an-Nahw, Makhazmi's an-Nahw al-caArab:Naqdun waTawjhun and Ibn Madha's Ar-Radd cal al-Nut; selected topics of Arabic Grammar, such as the Construct, the Appositives, Exception, the Adverb

courses.title: The Writings of Nigerian Ulama
skills_learned: explain the history and development of Arabic in Nigeria
identify the influence of Magrib on Nigerian Arabic New Arts                   45
selected topics and texts from works of Nigerian authors in Arabic Language; and
be familiar with works of some notable Nigerian Arabists
courses.content_summary: Brief history of the advent of Arabic language into Nigeria; textual study of selected literary works of Nigerian authors such as Usman B. Fodio, Abdullahi B. Fodio, Muhammad Bello, Wazir Junaid and Abubakar Atiq for analysis, appreciation and comparison with similar works in the Arab World.

courses.title: Modern Arabic Poetry
skills_learned: be familiar with development of major modern schools of poetry; 2 identify the contribution Arabs in diaspora to modern Arabic poetry; and
be exposed to Arabic poetry
courses.content_summary: Advanced survey of the development of major modern schools of poetry and their representative selections. Contribution of Arabs in diaspora to modern Arabic poetry. The influence of European poetry on Arabic modern poetry. To study works of some poets like: Nazr Qabni, Badr shkir Assayyb, Nzik Al-malikah, Mahmd Darwsh, Jibrn Khall Jibrn etc.

courses.title: Modern Arabic Prose
skills_learned: identify the development of major modern schools of prose
identify the influence, of translation on modern Arabic prose
discuss advantage and disadvantage of present mass- media on modern Arabic prose; and
be exposed to representative selections of modern Arabic prose
courses.content_summary: Survey of the growth and development of modern Arabic prose; representative selections from the works of novelists, playwrights and essayists. Influence of translation on modern Arabic prose. Advantage and disadvantage of present mass- media on modern Arabic prose should be studied in this course.

courses.title: Selected Topics in Arabic Grammar
skills_learned: develop critical approach to Arabic grammar, and
analyse various views of scholars on Arabic grammar New Arts                                        46
criticize the call for substituting classical Arabic with Modern Arabic dialects; 4. explain the views of those who call for easing Arabic grammar and the contrary; and
analyse the views of other scholars who insist on sticking to traditional grammar
courses.content_summary: Selected topics in Arabic Grammar; Views of Ibn Madha' Alqrtub, Ahmad `Amn, Shawq Daif, and their call for easing Arabic grammar should be studied. Also views of other scholars who insist on sticking to traditional grammar are to be surveyed. The call for substituting classical Arabic with Modern Arabic dialects, advantages and disadvantages to be discussed.

courses.title: Introduction to Arabic Lexicography
skills_learned: explain the historical background to the development of Arabic Lexicography;
appreciate types of Arabic dictionary; and
use and analyse different types of dictionaries
courses.content_summary: Historical background to the development of Arabic Lexicography, through different periods of time, the Schools of the Arabic Lexicon; the study of some old and modern dictionaries, according to order of lexicons entries i.e. the phonetic order, the last letter order and the alphabetic order. Also to be studied is the Language Academies and their efforts in development of Arabic dictionaries. Some

courses.title: Rhetoric II
skills_learned: analyse advance areas of Arabic rhetoric
discuss new ideas and approaches to Arabic Rhetoric
discover Jurjn's theory of Nadhm in his two books "Addal'il wa Al-`asrr"; and
analayse relationship between rhetoric and semantic and other sciences
courses.content_summary: The study of the "Badc'" Aspect of Arabic Rhetoric as (Jins, Sajac, Tibq, Muqbala, Tawriyah, usnu tacll and Mublagah) as well as discussions on new ideas or approaches to Arabic and Rhetoric.

courses.title: Applied Linguistics
skills_learned: identify the basics of Applied Linguistics, including error analysis and contrastive analyses
discuss modern ideas and approaches to teaching of Arabic language as second language, and
courses.content_summary: Introduction to the concept of applied linguistics, the science of error analysis and contrastive Analyses; The importance of applied linguistics in Arabic studies and its teaching as a second language, and recent innovations in this field, efforts of notable scholars in Applied Linguistics and contributions of some major centres of teaching Arabic to non- speakers in Arab world i.e. University of

courses.title: Translation II
skills_learned: use and edit machine translation
courses.content_summary: Advanced types of translation from and into Arabic. intensive exercises include using and editing machine translation.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship for Arabic
skills_learned: discover available chances for Arabic graduate in government, private sector, and
secure self-employment by opening his Arabic school
design and start business related to Arabic in computer, commerce, teaching; and
master the arts of Arabic calligraphy and translation
courses.content_summary: This will provide a wide survey of chances for Arabic graduate and avail him to available vacancies, in government, private sector and self-employment. These include foreign affairs, journalism, Arabic computer typesetting, teaching, translation and interpretation. Training the student on Arabic calligraphy and other art works dependent on Arabic language expertise, i.e. writing Quranic verses.

produce a research work of reasonable length
exhibit ability to design and carry out research and present an original piece of writing in the programme; and

explore conference presentation and publication supervisor should first ask the student write and defend a proposal. courses.content_summary: The meaning of archaeology and its basic aims. Origin and growth of archaeology as a discipline with particular reference to Africa. Principles and techniques of archaeology. Site prospection in archaeology. Dating methods in archaeology. Archaeology and development.

skills_learned: identify the different stages of archaeological development in the new world and characterise each;

identify and characterise the major civilizations of the new world and argue how and why they collapsed; and
understand the extent to which the environment played a major role in the rise and collapse of civilizations in the new word.
courses.content_summary: A survey of New world geography and paleo ecology. The peopling of the New world. The different stages of cultural development in the New world ( the lithic, archaic, formative, classic and post classic). Food production in the New world. Civilizations of the New world. Energy capture in the New world.

courses.title: Archaeology of Africa
skills_learned: clearly argue out how africa is the cradle of humankind
analyse how agriculture and metallurgy led to the development of complex societies in africa;
identify the significance of the nile valley, east and southern africa in the archaeology of the continent; and
explain the bantu problematic and the different lines of inquiry used in bantu studies
courses.content_summary: The African paleo environment. Language families in Africa. Africa and human origins. Stone Age cultures of Africa. Food production in Africa. Egypt and the Nile valley. The African Iron Age and Bantu migrations.

explain the history of archaeology, when and how it emerged as a scientific discipline

know the different theories and models of explanation in archaeology
courses.content_summary: The nature of archaeological evidence. How archaeological sites are formed. The history of archaeology and how it became a modern science. Ownership and stewardship of archaeological resources. Ethical

courses.title: Quaternary Studies and Archaeology
courses.content_summary: The Quaternary as a geological time period. Basics of Quaternary archaeology. Pleistocene and Holocene environments and their impact on our physical environment, eco systems, climate and culture. Quaternary sciences and human origins.

courses.title: Field Archaeology

courses.content_summary: The course is both theoretical and practical covering the following topics: Laws, ethics and safety in field archaeology. Survey and reconnaissance techniques in archaeology. Surface collection techniques. Field photography and illustrations. Elementary use of survey equipment. Map reading and map making. Excavation techniques. Stratigraphic profiles and the Harris Matrix.

argue how micro and macro organisms affect the preservation of archaeological remains

carry out systematic interpretation and analysis of film There are three components to this course: Film history Exploration of the journey of the cinema in Nigeria, beginning from the celluloid-era through the transformation into video and into cinema exhibition and internet streaming. The emergent characteristics of the Nollywood film. Notable creative pioneers and their contributions, as well as the relationship of film to other media. Film theory Film as a complex cultural medium. Realist theory. Genre theory. Auteur theory. Structuralism. Feminist theory. How artistic modes and theories situate the filmmaker; the film; the audience. Film criticism Exploration of critical approaches to narrative, non-narrative films, as well as critical lenses such as genre, authorship, and ideology with which motion pictures can be analyzed. Analyses of mise-en-sc�ne, cinematography, editing, and sound in motion pictures. Examination of the social, cultural, and political contexts of motion pictures as a medium. Systematic interpretation and analysis of film/motion pictures. Main topic areas: motion picture formal systems: [narrative/narration; rhetorical and categorical; associational abstract] motion picture stylistic systems: [aspects of mise-en-sc�ne; properties of cinematography; dimensions of editing; properties of sound]; analysis of style; basic approaches to motion picture analysis [cultural analysis; race; gender]; genre analysis and authorship analysis. Screenings.

courses.title: Peace and Conflict Resolution
skills_learned: analyse the concepts of peace, conflict and security
list major forms, types and root causes of conflict and violence
differentiate between conflict and terrorism
enumerate security and peace building strategies; and

describe roles of international organisations, media and traditional institutions in peace building Concepts of peace, conflict and security in a multi-ethnic nation. Types and theories of conflicts: ethnic, religious, economic, geo-political conflicts. Structural conflict theory, realist theory of conflict, frustration-aggression conflict theory. Root causes of conflict and violence in Africa: indigene and settlers phenomena; boundary/boarder disputes; political disputes; ethnic disputes and rivalries. Economic inequalities; social dispute. Nationalist movements and agitations. Selected conflict case studies � Tiv-Junkun; Zango Kartaf. Chieftaincy and land disputes, etc. Peace building, management of conflicts and security. Peace and human development. Approaches to eace & conflict management --- (religious, government, community leaders etc.). elements of peace studies and conflict resolution. Conflict dynamics assessment scales. Constructive and destructive, justice and legal framework. Concepts of social justice; the Nigerian legal system. Insurgency and terrorism. Peace mediation and peace keeping. Peace and Security Council (international, national and local levels). Agents of conflict resolution � conventions, treaties, community policing. evolution and imperatives. Alternative New Arts 283 Dispute Resolution (ADR). Dialogue, arbitration, negotiation, collaboration, etc. Roles of international organizations in conflict resolution - (a). the United Nations (UN) and its conflict resolution organs; the African Union and Peace Security Council. ECOWAS in peace keeping. The media and traditional institutions in peace building. Managing post-conflict situations; refugees. Internally Displaced Persons (IDPS). The role of NGOs in post-conflict situations.

skills_learned: demonstrate good understanding of Hausa verbs; 2 distinguish between verbs and verbals; and

Syllabic structure (the mono-syllabic and di-syllabic verbs of the Language).

courses.title: Introductory Grammar
skills_learned: explain various parts of speech; and
decipher the syntactical functions of such aspects
courses.content_summary: The course, which is preliminary, deals with the concepts of parts of speech in general and in Hausa. The course therefore studies parts of speech such as nouns, adjectives, verbs and adverbs and their syntactical functions.

courses.title: Orthography of Hausa
skills_learned: exhibit good grasp of the evolution and development of Hausa orthography; 2 explain the justification for, and functions of orthography; and
appreciate the desirability of orthography for any language
courses.content_summary: The general principles and practice in Orthography. Evolution and development of in Hausa. Types of Orthography. Justification for Orthography. Functions of Orthography. Survey of Orthographies of Hausa.

explain and apply contemporary theories in critiquing Hausa poetry
courses.content_summary: Nature as well as the main issues in the study and appreciation of Hausa poetry. Introduction to the basic terms and concepts of Hausa poetry. Criticism of Hausa poetry (pays particular attention to both oral and written poetry). The essential nature and common features of the two traditions of verse and their distinguishing characteristics, as well as their mutual influences. Aspects of history,

courses.title: Introduction to Linguistics
skills_learned: exhibit background understanding of Linguistics and related concepts; and 2 demonstrate clear understanding of the basic structure of language.
courses.content_summary: This course seeks to explain what Linguistics is, its scope, its application as well as to examine Language, its structure, its nature. The course will as well introduce students to acoustic phonetics and a study of the non-segmental features of speech such as pitch, tone, stress, and intonation.

courses.title: Introduction to Narratology
skills_learned: identify the basic classification and types of Hausa narratives; 2 explain the rudiments and skills of appreciating narratives; 3. demonstrate the ability to create narratives.
courses.content_summary: This course introduces students to the study and appreciation of narratives, oral and literate, long and short, simple and complex, and the various indigenous sub types. Students will also be encouraged to produce creative as well as natural narratives in oral as well as in written form.

courses.title: Introduction to Drama
skills_learned: identify the basic classification and types of Hausa Drama
explain the rudiments and skills of appreciating Hausa Drama
distinguish between the Hausa traditional and Modern Drama; and
explain the relationship between dramatic performances, and with other genres New Arts 303
courses.content_summary: The course is designed to introduce students to both traditional and modern Hausa Drama. Their various backgrounds, developments and types will be treated. The relationship between drama and other dramatic performances as with other literary genres will be studied.

courses.title: Pre-Danfodio Literature
skills_learned: explain the relevance of literary history
identify and examine the factors responsible for dearth of written literary materials in hausa prior to the debut of danfodio; and
appreciate the efforts of literary historians in unearthing some literary resources that were hitherto unavailable.
courses.content_summary: The course aims at drawing student's attention to this sparsely documented area of Hausa literary history as well as identifying and examining the factors responsible for this. Evaluation of the merits of scholarly works.

explain and apply the acquired knowledge of prosody in examining written Hausa poetry
courses.content_summary: The course aims at introducing students to the science of rhyme in written prosody. Commencing with a background survey of the metrical slots in Hausa poetry, the course further critically examines the poetic marriage and or the influence of prosodic and metric traditions of other languages over that of the Hausa.

courses.title: Hausa Thought and Literature
skills_learned: decipher, through the study of literature, the Hausa thought and worldview; 2 debunk the Eurocentric conception that African do not have worldview; and
to hold in high esteem their African pedigree

explain the functions and the processes of, as well as the techniques involved in translation as espoused by different scholars. including interpretation.

explain the processes of translation as demonstrated by different scholars; and
demonstrate ability to translate simple texts from english to hausa and vice-versa
courses.content_summary: Practical application of the theories of translation already learnt. Texts of different sizes covering diverse subjects in different styles are translated from and into the African Language and English.

identify and correct anomalies associated with the language of the social media
courses.content_summary: The course principally focuses on the use of Hausa Language in the media. skills_learned: evaluate modern Hausa prose, taking into cognizance the western and traditional theories and techniques; and
explain the underlying reasons for the evolution of this category of Literature, its theme, style and the effect of globalization on them.

courses.title: Hausa Contemporary Prose Fiction
skills_learned: evaluate modern Hausa prose, taking into cognizance the western and traditional theories and techniques; and
explain the underlying reasons for the evolution of this category of Literature, its theme, style and the effect of globalization on them.
courses.content_summary: The course will first study the background to the emergence from 80s of the private press category of novels and novelettes. It will also examine their predominantly romantic nature, the largely youthful character of both the artists and audience as well as the impact of these on the style.

courses.title: Issues in Hausa Phonology
skills_learned: demonstrate good understanding of the principles of generative phonology, the theory of distinctive features (the treatment of phonological processes), phonological representation and formulation of rules within the generative framework;
discuss the supra-segmental such as tone, intonation, vowel lengthening and shortening etc.; and

develop competence in phonetic description and phonetic classification of the sounds of Hausa Language, examination of their patterns of occurrence and distribution, discussion of contraction, (assimilation and features like tone, glide insertions, palatalization, neutralization and intonation).
courses.content_summary: The course attempts to discuss the current and relevant issues in phonology such as the generative framework to analyse the supra-segmentals of the Hausa language such as tones, vowel harmony, syllable structure, intonation, etc).

courses.title: Contemporary Hausa Poetry
skills_learned: demonstrate good knowledge of contemporary Hausa Oral and written poetry
apply theories of criticism to analyse the contemporary poetry; and
identify and explain the effect of globalization on the development of contemporary Hausa poetry from the thematic, stylistic and the cultural fronts.

courses.title: Issues in the Syntax of Hausa
skills_learned: understand and develop competence on the basic tenets of syntactic analysis and syntactic processes like deletion, movement, complementation, subordination in Hausa etc.; New Arts 315
describe the relations within the Hausa sentence: subject, predicate, object, adjunct, tense, aspect, mood number; and

courses.content_summary: A consideration of the current and relevant issues in the syntax of Hausa such as tense, aspect, and their relationships, ideophones; pronominalization, relativization, and reflexivization, nominalization adjectives would be pursued.

courses.title: Advanced Ajami

courses.content_summary: This course involves a detailed study of the Ajami graphemes or graphology. Also to be studied are standard and substandard Ajami and its dialectal and ideolectal fluctuations. There will also be practice on text analysis and transliteration, in addition to the use of innovations.

courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Hausa Film and Drama
skills_learned: demonstrate knowledge and understanding of film in general and Hausa film in particular
decipher the mutating nature of the themes, styles, characters as well as plots in contemporary Hausa film; and
explain the extent of the influence of Globalization and its agents on the cultural and literary settings of contemporary Hausa film.
courses.content_summary: The course examines the recent developments in television drama that led to the emergence of what is popularly known as Home Video Drama. The socio-economic factors that gave birth to this phenomenon are studied. The differences between this new category of drama and the previous ones are discussed in relation to copyright, production, plot, characters and themes.

courses.content_summary: The role of early Muslim philosophers and their contributions to the development of Islamic culture and civilization. Studies of selected Muslim philosophers of Middle Eastern and Western (Spanish) origin such as as al-Kind, Ibn Rushdi, al-Ghazl and al-Mridn.

courses.title: Islamic Family Law
skills_learned: explain the Islamic teachings with regards to marriage
appreciate the importance that Islam attaches to marriage as an institution of procreation, socialization and character building;
practicalize the Islamic teachings for the preservation of family values, and
guide, advice and adjudicate on Islamic family issues
courses.content_summary: The concept of marriage from Islamic perspective. Courtship in Islam. The marital contract. Elements which constitute a valid marriage contract. Impediments to marriage. Divorce in Islam. Polygamy in Islam. Guardianship and paternity. Family planning and birth control.

courses.title: Sources and Development of the Sharicah
skills_learned: describe the basic elements of Islamic law
recognize the existence of diversity and plurality within Islamic law
refute misconceptions about Islam, and 4. reconcile jurisprudential and legal differences
courses.content_summary: New Arts 401 The meaning and concept of the Sharcah. The primary sources of Sharcah. The secondary sources of Sharcah. The pre-Islamic Arab customs and the reforms introduced by Islam. The development of the Sharcah (Islamic law). The Sunni and Shcite Schools of Law.

courses.title: History of Islam from the Four Rightly-guided Caliphs to the cAbbsid
skills_learned: discuss with authority issues of Islamic history
explain the need for each Muslim to contribute towards the development of Islam and its civilization.
appreciate the history of Islam and the contributions of different categories of people towards its development and civilization;
explain and adopt the best and exemplary qualities of the Prophet (saw) and other pious Muslims; and
discuss Islamic history, authoritatively
courses.content_summary: The biography of the four rightly-guided caliphs, Abubakar, Umar, Uthman, Ali. The developmental patterns of Islamic civilization during their time. The rise and fall of the Ummayad. The cAbbsid dynasty. The specific contributions of the two eras to Islamic history.

courses.title: Textual Studies of the Qur'n I
skills_learned: read Islamic texts in Arabic language
analyze Islamic texts
pass sound judgment on them; and
demonstate capacity in Islamic jurisprudence
courses.content_summary: A detailed study of the recitation, translation, commentaries and teachings of the following Qur'nic chapters (suwar): al-Ftihah, an-Ns, al-Muzammil, al-Muddaththir and al-cAlaq

courses.title: Textual studies of the adthI
skills_learned: read Islamic texts in the source language
analyze Islamic texts
pass sound judgment on them, and New Arts 402
exhibit competence in Islamic jurisprudence
courses.content_summary: A detailed study on the reading, translation, commentaries and teachings of the Prophet on some selected ahdth, especially those relevant to contemporary daily life: adths on sincerity, repentance, perseverance, truthfulness, piety, firm belief, steadfastness, hypocrites, neighbourliness, parents.

courses.title: Islam and Gender Studies
skills_learned: appreciate one's gender
explain the Islamic teachings regarding each gender's responsibilities
promote gender equity
appreciate the position of Islam with regards to women education, and
compare the teachings of Islam with current practices
courses.content_summary: The position of women before Islam. Islamic provisions on gender equity with regards to both sexes. The Prophet's examples and teachings on women, modesty and hijb. Role of men and women in society. Women education. Evaluation of gender relationship in the Muslim world today whether in accordance with the teachings of the Qur'n and Sunnah. 300 Level

Social integrative theory, gender theory, inter-culturality theory, liberation theory, etc.Theoretical underpinnings as the essential foundation of humanities scholarship.Evaluation of the merits of scholarly works.

skills_learned: read Islamic texts in Arabic language
translate and analyze Islamic texts
pass sound judgment on them; and

translate and analyze Islamic texts on challenges of life and living

courses.content_summary: A detailed study of some selected adths, especially those relevant to daily life from Sahih Bukhr and Muslim.

Doctrine of Majlis al-cAqd: formulation of contract, contracting parties and subject matter of contract. Islamic teachings on ownership of wealth, usury, interest, banking, insurance, gambling, labour and relevance of these to modern situations.

courses.title: Sharcah: Al-cUqbt

exhibit competence in Islamic jurisprudence
explain the Islamic rulings with regards to murder, theft, intoxicants and slander, and
comment on some chapters of the Qur'n
courses.content_summary: A study of Islamic regulations on murder, theft, intoxicant, Qadhf (slander); with emphasis on relevance of these regulations to morality. Comprehensive study on some selected portions of Surah al-Nr (Chapter 24) and Surah al-Azb(Chapter 33).

courses.title: History and Creed of Ahlul-Sunnah and the Shicah
skills_learned: explain the doctrinal diversity and pluralism within Islam
reconcile differences of opinion in the practice and interpretation of Islam, and 3 refute misconceptions that may arise from some scholars' understanding of Islam.
courses.content_summary: Doctrines and principles of Ahl al-Sunnah. The classes of Ahl al-Sunnah. Their roles in Muslim communities. Their major leaders and their training. The Shcah: definition, doctrines, divisions, location and impact of their activities.

courses.title: Entrepreneurial Skills

appreciate the position of Islam with regards to entrepreneurial skills

The concept of calligraphy: meaning, etymology and history of calligraphy. Purpose, types and tools for calligraphy. Practical teaching of different aspects of calligraphy, such as, graphic designs, paintings, cut stone inscriptions, wedding

courses.title: Moral Philosophy in Islam

appreciate the importance that Islam attaches to good moral conduct New Arts 407
appreciate the Islamic teachings with regards to morality, and
adopt the good conduct as exemplified by the Prophet (saw) and other pious Muslims
courses.content_summary: The concept and importance of morality and ethics. The moral teachings in the Qur`n. The Prophet as Huswatun-Hasanah. Contributions of selected early Muslim scholars to moral thought: the Mutakallimn and Muaddithn, the Philosophers, and the Sufis. Muslim ethics in modern age in religion, law and morality.

courses.title: Islamic Political Thought and Movements

explain and appreciate the contributions of pre-modern Muslim intellectuals and scholars to Islamic Political Thought;
describe the rich repertoire of values and traditions within Islamic Political system; and
appraise the relevance of the Islamic Political Thought to contemporary period
courses.content_summary: Islam as a total way of life and government as an essential part of it. Principles of government in the Qur`n and adth. Historical and intellectual development of government in Islam. Political institutions: al-Wizrah, al-Khilfah, al-Mazlim, al-Hisbah. Political thought of the Jihad movement of Shaikh cUthman bn Fu di. Encounter of Islam with Western imperialism. 400 Level

courses.title: Fiqh of Contemporary Issues
skills_learned: discuss, with authority on Islamic jurisprudence
give legal opinions on Islamic judicial matters, especially on contemporary issues
explain contemporary trends and streams in economics and other socio-political aspects of life, and
present authentic Islamic position on contemporary issues
courses.content_summary: The Islamic ethical teachings and fiqh of some contemporary issues in Islamic Bio-ethics such as cloning, euthanasia, suicide, capital punishment, terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and crypto- currency.

courses.title: Advanced Study of Muslim Law
skills_learned: give legal opinions on Islamic judicial and legal matters
reconcile differences of opinion on the practices or interpretations of Islamic law
appreciate the dynamics and trajectories in legal traditions in Islam, and
explain the foundational contributions of early Muslim jurists to Islamic legal heritage
courses.content_summary: Original sources of Muslim Law. Contributions of early companions to legal knowledge. Ijtid and Mujtahidn. The Sharicah in modern times. Modern reforms concerning marriage, divorce, inheritance. The principles of al-Siysah Shaciyyah, al-Tacsr, al-Takhayyur and al-Talfq. Recent demand for Sharcah in some Muslim countries. Muslim women and modern reforms.

courses.title: Islamic Contributions to the Renaissance

identify the contributions of Islam to western civilization and the development of modern Europe;
analyze the trajectories in the interface between Islam and the West, and

courses.content_summary: The concept of Renaissance in Islamic tradition. The position of Islam and its attitude to research and learning. Its contributions to the arts, sciences and other disciplines. History of the relationship between Islam and Western civilization. Islamic impact on Western Renaissance. Causes of the decline of Islamic civilization.

courses.title: Qdiriyyah and Tijniyyah
skills_learned: discuss Islamic mystical practices in Africa at large and in Nigeria in particular
appreciate the contributions of the Sufi Orders to Islamic heritage in Nigeria; 3 distinguish between their ideologies, and
discuss differences in Sufi practices
courses.content_summary: Brief account of the history of each of the Sufi groups. Their doctrines and rites. Social and political roles in Africa. Specific contributions of some Sufi leaders. Major Qdiriyyah and Tijniyyah settings, practices and leaders in Nigeria.

courses.title: Islam in Nigeria
skills_learned: appreciate the history of Islam in Nigeria
discuss the contributions of different categories of people towards its development and civilization;
explain the elements that constitute the penal system of Islamic law, and
differentiate between the penal court in Islam and common law
courses.content_summary: The spread and development of Islamic Institutions in Nigeria. Islam under colonial rule. A comparative study of the penal system (hudd) in Islam and the penal code in Northern Nigeria. Alkali and the Shar'ah courts in Nigeria.

courses.title: Islam and Pluralism
skills_learned: promote the values of inclusivity

identify the major events and centres of activities in each period
courses.content_summary: History and forms of Western music in some details from the death of Bach and Handel to the present. The course will be sub-divided into three main periods: (a) Classical, (b) Romantic, and (c) 20th Century. Notable composers and genres they are associated with. Major events and centres of activities in each period.

develop the skills to modulate into related keys
develop the skills to transpose; and
improvise freely in any style or musical type
courses.content_summary: Chord drills and harmonisation of melodies using the materials of MUS 121-123, 221-223, in four voice harmony and free style accompaniment. Detailed study of transposition, modulation and improvisation. New Arts 537

courses.title: SIWES

courses.title: Acoustics and Psycho-Acoustic of Music:
skills_learned: build appropriate and adequate concert hall and studio
identify the psychological aspects of music and its advanced tools
produce the desiderata for speech and music hall and studio; and
develop a solid foundation for continued learning in the area of interest
courses.content_summary: The Physics of musical sounds and musical instruments, sound waves, vibrations, fractional vibrations. Frequency, amplitude, phase, harmonics and harmonic series, formants, transients, consonance, dissonance. Thresholds of audibility, perception of change - pitch, volume, tone colour, psychological effects of acoustic features. Mathematical calculations of musical sound productions � just intonati

courses.title: Music Technology
skills_learned: construct and build a more complex musical instrument; 2. develop the skills to maintain and repair musical instruments; and New Arts 538
develop the higher skills of tuning the piano
courses.content_summary: The arts and science of constructing and building musical instruments. The concept and design, tools, materials, storage and maintenance, actual design and building of "original" instruments under the supervision of the instructor. Higher skills of Piano tuning.

courses.title: 20th Century Compositional Techniques
skills_learned: construct tone row and its various inversions
develop the skills to utilise different 20th Century compositional devices; and
analyse works of masters of 20th Century composition
courses.content_summary: Survey of the various processes of musical composition in the present era, using atonality, serialism, 12-tone, chance, electronic and computer techniques, among others. Examination of some works of the major composers of this century, such as Bartok, Stravinsky, Schonberg, Berg, Webern, Dallapiccola, etc.

courses.title: Fugue:
skills_learned: compose well defined exposition for 3-voice and 4-voice fugues
identify the compositional devices that are employed in the middle section of a fugue and
bring back home all the devices employed in the middle section and return home in the recapitulation with either a coda or codetta.
courses.content_summary: Application of the techniques of tonal counterpoint to fugal composition for students that choose Music Composition as their area of specialisation. Composition of 3-voice and 4-voice fugues. Compositional devices employed in the Middle Section of a fugue. Techniques employed in bringing back in the Recapitulation. Techniques of writing a coda or codetta.

courses.title: Orchestration:
skills_learned: identify the tonal registers of all musical instruments
identify various conventions of notation
engage manuscript layout intelligibly; and New Arts 539
engage in reduction of orchestral pieces for medium ensembles or enlarge piano pieces for large ensembles such as military band and symphony orchestra.
courses.content_summary: Study of instrumentation with an examination of the possibilities and limitations of the commonly used Western orchestra instruments. Conventions of notation, scoring and arranging for various ensembles, small, medium and large. Exercises to include both Western orchestral and African instruments.

courses.title: Analysis and Analytic Method for 20th Century Music
skills_learned: engage contemporary tools of analysis for post-tonal music
apply the computers techniques for the analysis of various styles of 20th Century music and
analyse works of masters of 20th Century composition
courses.content_summary: An examination of some contemporary tools of analysis for post-tonal music, including the set complex theory. The application of computers techniques for the analysis of music in general.

courses.title: Composition:
skills_learned: compose original works of different styles � both Western and African musical traditions; 2 develop the skills to utilise different types of musical instruments;
analyse works of traditional African musicians as well as those of masters of all periods of Western music history.
courses.content_summary: Musical creativity and composition for voices and instruments. Various styles and genres � both Western and African � emphasis on musically logical use of Western and African compositional devices. Judicious use of different styles of instrumental combination.

courses.title: Special Topic in the History of Western Music:
skills_learned: synthesise the various aspects of musical genres or musical types taken previously
develop a critical thinking
produce objective argument; and
develop a high level of music appreciation New Arts 540
courses.content_summary: Topics will include Bach, Haydn and Mozart, Beethoven, Chamber Music, The Symphony, The Concerto, Opera, English, Church Music. The Development of the Pianoforte, 20th Century Composers, etc.

courses.title: Historiography of Music:
skills_learned: develop the techniques for documenting the history of music
develop a critical thinking
produce objective argument; and
develop a high level of music appreciation
courses.content_summary: Development of techniques for documenting the history of music. Methods of documenting history of music. Types of documentation. The use of archival materials for documentation. Music appreciation.

courses.title: African Music III:
skills_learned: synthesise the various aspects of musical elements, genres or musical types of African music taken previously;
produce objective argument; and
develop a high level of music appreciation
courses.content_summary: Quality of the music of the peoples of black Africa. An analysis of its theoretical peculiarities with special reference to form, rhythm, melody and scales, harmony, and instrumentation. Problems of notation and transcription.

courses.title: Contemporary African Music:
skills_learned: develop requisite skills to cope with the trends in contemporary African music
develop the requisite for objective argument on composed art music and popular music and
develop a high level of music appreciation
courses.content_summary: New Arts 541 Trends in contemporary African music, including composed art music and popular music. Objectives and techniques employed by African art music composers, and influences leading to the music of today in Africa. Contemporary music makers and their works.

courses.title: Key-Board Harmony and Accompaniment
skills_learned: accompany all categories of styles of vocal and instrumental groups and solos
develop the requisite skills for realisation in accompanying solo and group performances; 3. develop much higher skills to modulate freely; and
improvise freely in any style or musical type
courses.content_summary: Harmonisation of melodies and free style accompaniment, accompanying of vocal and instrumental groups and solos. Modulation from different keys freely - both major or minor. Improvisation in any style or musical type. Keyboard skills for the classroom teacher will be facilitated.

courses.title: School Music Methods:
skills_learned: develop various methods of teaching music at all levels
analyse and interpret musical works (performance and composition) effectively; and
develop the ability to impart the knowledge of theoretical and practical areas of music
courses.content_summary: Methods of teaching music in the Primary, Secondary and teacher training institutions, with particular reference to Nigeria. Analysis and interpretation of musical works (either performance or composition. Imparting knowledge of theoretical and practical areas of music.

courses.title: Teaching and Supervision of Instrumental Music
skills_learned: impart the knowledge of ensemble performance
combine musical instruments of different sections of the orchestra in a musically logical manner;
identify the peculiarities of musical instruments with regard to transposition; and
develop the principle of teaching and supervising instrumental music New Arts 542
courses.content_summary: Basic orchestra and band instruments (and of one in particular), with a view to equipping the student with the principles and practice of teaching and supervising instrumental music at all levels. Transposing instruments and their intervals of transposition.

courses.title: African Music in Schools:
skills_learned: develop a critical thinking
produce objective argument; and
develop a high level of music appreciation
courses.content_summary: This is a seminar class to discuss and discover solutions to the problems of adopting African music for Schools as well as composition and research procedures. Engagement of issues such as tuning and tuning system, improvisation, and performance techniques.

courses.title: Criticism and Musical Scholarship
skills_learned: evaluate musical performances, composition, and scholarly works; 2 harmonise and employ Western and African aesthetics; and
develop interdisciplinary horizon
courses.content_summary: Theory of Western Aesthetics in the humanities and its relevance and application to Africa. Evaluation of works and performances, and the communication of this evaluation in good literary style. The bibliography and style, the writing for scholarly journals, editing of articles and scores. Key to Courses Acoustics and Music Technology; 0 General Courses (Rudiments); 1 Theoretical Courses � Harmony

explain the gradual evolution of Nigeria as a political unit

analyse the role of the Judiciary in upholding people's fundamental rights
identify acceptable norms and values of the major ethnic groups in Nigeria; and
list and suggest possible solutions to identifiable Nigerian environmental, moral and value problems.
courses.content_summary: New Arts 551 Nigerian history, culture and art up to 1800 (Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo peoples and culture; peoples and culture of the ethnic minority groups). Nigeria under colonial rule (advent of colonial rule in Nigeria; colonial administration of Nigeria). Evolution of Nigeria as a political unit (amalgamation of Nigeria in 1914; formation of political parties in Nigeria; Nationalist movement and

courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.content_summary: The inevitability of Philosophy (why study Philosophy?); the nature and meaning of Philosophy (Philosophy as worldview; Philosophy as critical thinking; Philosophy as rational enquiry; Philosophy as reconstruction of ideas). Styles and methods of Philosophy. A brief survey of the branches of Philosophy. Current trends in Philosophical Thoughts, etc

courses.title: Arguments and Critical Thinking
skills_learned: the explain nature of arguments
identify flaws in arguments
develop the capacity to differentiate between valid and invalid arguments, and

acquire the habit of critical thinking Course Ccontents Nature of arguments. Validity and invalidity. Definitions, formal and informal fallacies. Deductive and inductive arguments, etc. Structured arguments and differentiation between logical and illogical reasoning. New Arts 552

courses.title: Elementary Ethics
skills_learned: explain the basic ethical concepts of good, bad, right and wrong
have a grasp of the grounds upon which certain actions are judged to be right and others as wrong, and
imbibe the positive effect of such knowledge/capacity in his/her conduct
courses.content_summary: This course introduces the students to Axiology, the Philosophy of Values; it examines some of the fundamental principles of Ethics; involves a brief introduction to the major ethical theories; definitions of good, bad, right and wrong; the principles of justice and conscience. Knowing what is good and doing what is good, etc.

courses.title: History of Philosophy
courses.content_summary: An examination of the origins of major philosophical thoughts and ideas, from ancient times to medieval period and contemporary times. Philosophers for analysis include the preSocratics: Thales, Anaximander, Anaximenes, the Sophists, etc. Others are: Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, St Thomas Aquinas, Hegel, Kant, Locke, Humes, Descartes and Karl Marx, A. J Ayer, Fukuyama, etc. Major African Philosophe

courses.title: Introduction to Social and Political Philosophy
courses.content_summary: New Arts 553 The State and the citizen. The nature of man and the origins of the state. The concepts of political obligation. The ideal state and the individual. History of political thought and some of the existing political theories, from ancient to modern times. From Athenian democracy to contemporary Social and Political theories. Politics, the state and the African experience.

courses.title: Introduction to African Philosophy
courses.content_summary: Is there an African Philosophy? What is Philosophy as a general concept? The debate on the existence or otherwise of African Philosophy: what qualifies a discipline to be Philosophy? Traditional versus contemporary African Philosophy. Are there universal criteria for identifying African Philosophy? Methodologies and orientations in African Philosophy. Contemporary doctrines in African Philosophy.

courses.title: Oriental Philosophies
courses.content_summary: What is an Oriental Philosophy? Major Oriental Philosophies in the world. Methods, orientations and insights into Oriental Philosophies. Instances of Oriental Philosophies: Buddhist, Hindu and Confucian Philosophies. Unique features of Oriental systems of logic, world-views, religions, cultures, social institutions, politics and ethics. A comparative analysis of Oriental Philosophies with other ma

courses.title: Ancient Philosophy
courses.content_summary: The beginnings of Western Philosophy, from the Pre-Socratics to Roman times. Original issues raised by Ancient Philosophers. Fusion of subject matter: cosmology, epistemology and ethics. The doctrines of Graeco-Roman Philosophers � e.g. Thales, Anaximander, Anaximenes, etc. Evolution of philosophical ideas, from ancient to modern times. 200 Level
